newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Law recognising poll wins goes to Serbia assembly.
newsitem.headline: Law recognising poll wins goes to Serbia assembly.

text.p: The Serbian government approved on Wednesday a draft law reinstating disputed results of local elections and sent it to parliament, the official Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported.

Serbia's opposition, students and professional groups have mounted 78 days of massive, relentless rallies demanding that their municipal election wins on November 17 in 14 towns and cities, including the capital, be reinstated.
The victories were annulled by the ruling Socialists, who cited unspecified "irregularities".
Quoting the Serbian Information Ministry, Tanjug said the government accepted that Serbia's relations with the OSCE and the international community outweighed the importance of any electoral dispute.
On Tuesday, autocratic Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic suddenly announced that he would ask parliament to reinstate the disputed results.
Two days earlier, Milosevic had sent in his paramilitary police to break up relentless opposition protests. Repeated baton charges injured scores of people and prompted an international outcry.

Milosevic's critics at home and abroad have reacted to his decision with caution. Washington called it a step in the right direction and France urged Belgrade to take concrete steps toward recognising the opposition wins.

The opposition said it would continue protests until its demands were implemented. Opposition parties also want free media and an independent judiciary ahead of parliamentary and presidential elections due by the end of this year.

The 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, from which Yugoslavia has been suspended, verified that the opposition Zajedno coalition won the municipal vote without "irregularities".
State television said parliament would meet to consider the draft law next Tuesday.
